tspan.tspan: a citizen science macroinvertebrate survey tool that now teaches taxonomy

text.tspan: John Gooderham - The National Waterbug Blitz
Justine Holmes - WaterWatch Victoria, Corangamite Catchment Management Authority, Colac, Victoria, Australia
Paul Feely - Centre for eResearch and Digital Innovation, Federation University, Ballarat, Victoria, Australia
Birgita Hansen - Centre for eResearch and Digital Innovation, Federation University, Ballarat, Victoria, Australia

tspan.tspan: Aspiring citizen scientists can use the YouTube training material and follow along
in the Academy feature. The videos describe how to characterise the taxa and
give a set of test identifications. In the app, creatures are identified via a guided
dichotomous key illustrated with photos and video. When a user misidentifies a
taxon, they are returned to the key at the question they answered incorrectly so

text.tspan: they can learn from their mistakes.

tspan.tspan: When a citizen scientist is sufficiently proficient at identification they can use the survey
functionality within the app in the field. The dichotomous key uses a taxonomy that has
been created specifically to require only a magnifying glass to get reliable field
identifications. There is also a speed bug screen that allows shortcutting the key when

text.tspan: the user is familiar with the creature's silhouette.

tspan.tspan: Citizen science waterbug surveys face competing demands: the identification task must be
achievable by participants without formal training, while the resulting data must still be
scientifically useful. The Waterbug App is a free mobile application designed around that tension
rather than resolving it in favour of one side.
After a survey is completed it is submitted to the server, where a
SIGNAL score is calculated, the site’s historical survey data is displayed,

text.tspan: and the proportional land use upstream of the site is calculated.
